_comment: Database advisor findings we have reviewed and accepted, keyed by the cache_key splinter emits.
Anything firing in a gated category that is NOT listed here fails CI, so a newly introduced
SECURITY DEFINER function or exposed table is caught rather than lost in the noise.
The Supabase dashboard has no dismiss feature, which is why this file exists.
Every entry needs a reason. If a reason no longer holds, fix the finding instead of keeping it here.

ignored_rules.name: multiple_permissive_policies
ignored_rules.reason: Performance advisory, not a security finding: several permissive policies on one table mean Postgres evaluates each on every query. Real, but a separate optimization workstream and currently 390 findings. Reported by the runner, not gated.

ignored_rules.name: auth_rls_initplan
ignored_rules.reason: Performance advisory: auth.uid() re-evaluated per row instead of once per query. Worth fixing in bulk with the policies above, not a reason to block a deploy.

ignored_rules.name: unindexed_foreign_keys
ignored_rules.reason: Performance advisory about covering indexes. Adding indexes blindly to satisfy a linter costs write throughput, so these get judged against real query plans instead.

ignored_rules.name: unused_index
ignored_rules.reason: Performance advisory. Reports indexes with no recorded scans, which on a young production database mostly means the query has not run yet rather than that the index is useless.

ignored_rules.name: duplicate_index
ignored_rules.reason: Performance advisory, single occurrence. Worth tidying, never worth failing a build.

ignored_rules.name: pg_graphql_anon_table_exposed
ignored_rules.reason: Local-stack artifact, not a production finding. The Supabase CLI installs pg_graphql by default; production does not have the extension at all (checked pg_extension directly on 2026-08-16: no rows). These fire only against the local database CI builds. If GraphQL is ever enabled in production, drop this entry and work through the 111 findings properly, because then they become real.

ignored_rules.name: pg_graphql_authenticated_table_exposed
ignored_rules.reason: Same as the anon variant above: pg_graphql is present in the local CLI stack and absent in production, so these 120 findings do not describe the deployed system. Revisit if GraphQL is ever turned on.
